extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: An evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia, professionally translated into 101 languages, covering diverse topics and domains for multilingual machine translation evaluation.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.inLanguage: 101 languages including eng, spa, fra, deu, zho, ara, hin, rus, jpn, kor, and 91 others
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia, specifically from Wikinews (international news articles), Wikijunior (age-appropriate nonfiction books for children), and WikiVoyage (travel guide). The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia articles from Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentences were manually selected from Wikipedia articles, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences. For each sentence, metadata was extracted including Wikipedia URL, topic, and boolean flags indicating whether the sentence contained entities linked to other Wikipedia pages and images. All sentences were manually labeled by sub-topic.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Professional translators translated sentences through a carefully controlled process. For each language, all source sentences were sent to translation LSPs. Once translated, data was sent to different translators within the LSP for editing and then moved on to automated quality control steps. Translations were then sent to an evaluation LSP that performed quality assessment, providing a translation quality score and constructive linguistic feedback. If the score was below the accepted threshold (90%), translations were sent back for re-translation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was assessed through a Translation Quality Score calculated per language on a 0 to 100 scale, based on the number of identified errors by evaluation LSPs. Errors examined included: grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition or omission of information, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register. Each error was associated with a severity level between minor, major, and critical. The acceptable translation quality score was set to 90%.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One professional translation per sentence per language
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Professional translators from Language Service Providers. The sentence selection process was performed by 10 different annotators (6 male and 4 female) with different roles in research (researchers, scientists, engineers, program/project managers) originally coming from different regions: East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America and North America.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic checks were implemented including: language identification, checking whether the translation is a copy of the source sentence, checking whether the translation has significantly different length, checking translation fluency according to a language model, and checking whether the translation is a copy of the translation produced by publicly available translation engines.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dev and devtest splits are publicly downloadable. The test set will not be released but will be available via a publicly available evaluation server. The test set can be used by various evaluation campaigns, such as the WMT 2021 Large-Scale Multilingual Task.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to foster progress in machine translation for low-resource languages. The majority of the world's population speak low-resource languages and would benefit from improvements in translation quality on their native languages. The dataset enables evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems and supports regionally-relevant language pairs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: While translationese (overly literal or awkward translations) has known idiosyncrasies, the authors conjecture that these effects are rather marginal when evaluating models in low-resource languages. The source sentences are all from English Wikipedia, which may introduce bias as source sentences not in English are produced by human translators.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: All source sentences are extracted from English Wikipedia, meaning that source sentences not in English are produced by human translators (translationese). The dataset focuses on evaluation rather than training. Performance is heavily correlated with amount of training data available for each language. Translation between low-resource languages produces very low BLEU scores, indicating substantial room for improvement.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluation of machine translation systems, particularly for low-resource and multilingual translation. It supports evaluation of many-to-many translation (10,100 language pairs), document-level translation, and multimodal translation. Beyond translation, FLORES-101 can be used to evaluate tasks such as sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation. The dev set is for hyper-parameter tuning, devtest for testing during development, and test set for final evaluation via evaluation server.

The test set will not be released, but will be available via a publicly available evaluation server, while the dev and devtest are publicly downloadable. rai:dataLimitations.evidence: By translating the same set of English sentences in more than hundred languages, we enable evaluation of multilingual MT with the only caveat that source sentences not in English are produced by human translators... Performance is overall heavily correlated with amount of training data... Translation between very low and low-resource languages yields a mere spBLEU score of less than 5.
